Describe the differences between heterogeneous transition networks

Source: R/compare_htna.R
compare_htna.Rd

compare_htna() describes the differences between two heterogeneous transition networks, or between every pair of cohorts of a grouped network: overall, in how similar their weight matrices are, and in where the differences lie in the actor structure, within an actor (for example, how humans move between their own codes) or between actors (how the human hands over to the AI and back). It reports correlation, distance and similarity measures of the two weight matrices, the network-level metrics of each network, the difference of every edge, and a summary of the differences in each directed actor-pair block.

Networks that contain different subsets of the codes are aligned on the union of their codes, in actor order, with the missing codes treated as having no transitions; a code shared by both networks must belong to the same actor in both. Differences are x - y. compare_htna() runs Nestimate's compare_model() on the aligned networks and adds the actor-pair summary. It returns an htna_comparison object (an htna_comparison_group for a grouped network).

The comparison is descriptive and gives no test. Use permutation_htna() for a permutation test of the differences and bayes_compare_htna() for credible intervals; plot_htna_diff() draws the difference network. The tables of the result are returned by summary() and as.data.frame() (see htna_comparison-methods).

Usage

compare_htna(x, y = NULL, ...)

Arguments

x

An htna network, or an htna_group.

y

A second htna network; NULL (default) when x is an htna_group, in which case every pair of cohorts is compared.

...

Settings of the comparison: scaling, measures and network.

Value

For two networks, an object of class c("htna_comparison", "net_comparison"). For an htna_group, a named list of class c("htna_comparison_group", "list") with one comparison per cohort pair (for example "Early vs Late"). summary() returns the actor-pair table, one row per directed actor pair; as.data.frame(x, what = ) returns the actor-pair, edge, metric or network table (see htna_comparison-methods).

Conditions

Errors of class htna_bad_input when x and y are not htna networks, when y is given with an htna_group, or when the networks use different actor types; htna_empty_input when a group has fewer than two cohorts; htna_actor_conflict when a shared code belongs to different actors.

See also

htna_comparison-methods, permutation_htna(), bayes_compare_htna(), plot_htna_diff().

Examples

data(human_ai)
grp <- build_htna(human_ai, actor_type = "actor_type", group = "phase")
#> Metadata aggregated per session: ties resolved by first occurrence in 'cluster' (24 sessions), 'actor_type' (9 sessions)
#> Metadata aggregated per session: ties resolved by first occurrence in 'session_date' (1 sessions), 'cluster' (18 sessions), 'actor_type' (15 sessions)
comparison <- compare_htna(grp)
comparison
#> HTNA network comparisons: 1 cohort pair
#> 
#> --- Early vs Late ---
#>   Pearson correlation of edge weights: 0.959
#>   Mean absolute difference:            0.0192
#>  source target cells changed mean_diff mean_abs_diff max_abs_diff
#>   Human  Human    36      35   0.00168        0.0159       0.0631
#>   Human     AI    36      36  -0.00168        0.0179       0.0922
#>      AI  Human    36      36  -0.00622        0.0216       0.0571
#>      AI     AI    36      28   0.00622        0.0212       0.1810
summary(comparison)
#>      comparison source_actor target_actor n_cells n_nonzero_x n_nonzero_y
#> 1 Early vs Late        Human        Human      36          35          35
#> 2 Early vs Late        Human           AI      36          36          36
#> 3 Early vs Late           AI        Human      36          36          36
#> 4 Early vs Late           AI           AI      36          28          27
#>   n_changed mean_difference mean_absolute_difference rms_difference
#> 1        35     0.001681478               0.01593235     0.02279098
#> 2        36    -0.001681478               0.01791131     0.02767092
#> 3        36    -0.006221056               0.02158038     0.02683857
#> 4        28     0.006221056               0.02124805     0.04281287
#>   max_absolute_difference
#> 1              0.06311526
#> 2              0.09221141
#> 3              0.05710535
#> 4              0.18124427
